# AI Intelligence Briefing — 2026-11-02
**Coverage:** 2026-10-31T06:19:49Z–2026-11-02T06:19:49Z
**Generated:** 2026-11-02T06:19:49Z

## Executive Signals
- OpenAI cut the target for its latest funding round by about $10 billion, to roughly $20 billion at a $1.25 trillion post-money valuation, as AI stocks sold off. These are reported terms and the round has not closed — details in Section 6.
- Meituan released **LongCat-2.5**, a ~1.6-trillion-parameter multimodal model tuned for long-running agent work (Section 1).
- Apple confirmed **Apple Intelligence is coming to mainland China with Alibaba's Qwen** inside Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence, with a developer beta on 4 November (Section 4).
- Saudi Aramco **closed its purchase of 49% of the AI firm HUMAIN**, adding about $2.6 billion in cash plus AI assets while PIF keeps 51% (Section 6).
- South Korea proposed a record 2027 budget with about **$15.97 billion for AI, chips and "physical AI,"** nearly doubling last year's spend (Section 6).

## 1. Model Releases and Major Updates
| Date | Model / Organization | Status & Access | What Changed | Why It Matters | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-02 | LongCat-2.5 — Meituan | Released; online chat and API now, GitHub/Hugging Face releases to follow | ~1.6T total parameters with ~48B active (mixture-of-experts); first LongCat flagship to fold vision into the language backbone, with large-scale long-horizon reinforcement learning, a unified vision-text token framework and tasks built from real agent failures | Targets sustained agent tasks — long-horizon execution, tool use and visual coding — rather than single-turn benchmarks | [TechNode](https://technode.com/2026/11/02/meituan-launches-longcat-2-5-multimodal-ai-model-for-extended-coding-tasks/) · [longcat.ai](https://longcat.ai/) |
| 2026-11-01 | FineDNA + Carbon-X — Hugging Face Biology | Open (Apache-2.0); dataset plus a 14.8B model; runs on one 80GB GPU in bfloat16 | FineDNA publishes all three training stages behind Carbon-X, a Qwen3-14B model that takes raw DNA and answers in English: a 302B-token mid-training run from 514.3B tokens offered, 203,923 SFT conversations and 98,433 RL prompts with code-checkable answers | Rare to get the full recipe, not just weights; the verifiable-reward RL design is a template for any exact-answer field | [HF dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceBio/FineDNA) · [HF model](https://huggingface.co/HuggingFaceBio/Carbon-X) · [explainx](https://www.explainx.ai/blog/finedna-carbon-x-hugging-face-dna-dataset-300b-tokens-qwen3-14b-2026) |

| 2026-11-02 | Wizard: Manipulate Any World in Real Time via Agentic Control | Yuzhe Wu, Zijun Lin, Yeying Jin, Tencent | An agentic game world model that conditions a video generator on skeleton and geometry proxies plus adaptive masking; 50.3 hours of aligned proxy–video pairs over 750 scenes and 178 characters, running at 24 FPS with zero-shot generalisation | Real-time, fine-grained control of characters and scenes for player-built game worlds | Preprint (code forthcoming) | [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40339) · [Project](https://wyzardwu.github.io/wizard/) |

| 2026-11-01 | EditAgent (Adobe Research / UC San Diego) | Authors in paper; The Decoder attributes it to Adobe Research and UC San Diego | An image-editing agent that routes each step to specialized tools, generates parallel variants and hands a plain language model a "verification record" (close-ups, change maps, measured brightness and colour); experts preferred the parallel variants in 78.5% of decided comparisons, at ~10x compute | Suggests that giving a judge measurements can beat a fine-tuned judge — reusable for any agent that checks its own work | Preprint (arXiv 2610.39664) | [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39664) · [explainx](https://www.explainx.ai/blog/adobe-editagent-image-editing-agent-specialized-tools-verification-record-78-percent-10x-compute-2026) |
| 2026-11-01 | HairDeck | Yuze He, Yixiang Wei, Wang Zhao, Chuhao Chen, Yanning Zhou, Yong-Jin Liu (Tsinghua, CMU, CUHK) | Treats stylised hair as an unordered set of cards, one token each, generated with a set diffusion transformer followed by spring-bone chains; reports ~33x faster than CHARM (1.01s vs 33.7s) and 44% lower Chamfer error, with Apache-2.0 code and weights | Removes a slow hand-authored step in game and VRM characters, and shows set representations beat sequences for naturally unordered assets | Preprint | [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40599) · [GitHub](https://github.com/hyz317/HairDeck) |

## 5. AI Leader and Industry Watch
- **Sam Altman, OpenAI (2026-10-31):** Met about 50 Samsung Group executives in Yongin, South Korea, to deepen cooperation on memory chips and AI infrastructure as global memory shortages tighten. Sources: [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-31/openai-sam-altman-samsung-executives-memory-crunch-deepens) · [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/02/openai-sam-altman-samsung-sk-south-korea.html).
- **Elon Musk, xAI/SpaceX (2026-11-01):** Wrote on X that "the cost of serving Grok Bot was unsustainably high relative to revenue," replying to a user asking for a weekly-usage reset. He gave no figures, new limits or timeline. Sources: [Startup Fortune](https://startupfortune.com/elon-musk-admits-grok-bot-costs-too-much-to-run-as-users-hit-weekly-caps/) · [explainx](https://explainx.ai/blog/musk-grok-bot-serving-cost-unsustainably-high-weekly-usage-limits-what-is-verified-2026).
- **Andrej Karpathy, independent (2026-10-31):** Said Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Code built HackerTube (hackertube.org), a no-login site of 6,454 videos recommended in Hacker News comments since 2007, in about two hours; he published no token or dollar cost. Sources: [explainx](https://explainx.ai/blog/karpathy-hackertube-claude-opus-5-5-6454-videos-hacker-news-built-in-two-hours-2026) · [AI Weekly](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/karpathy-ships-hackertube-in-2-hours-with-claude-opus-55).

## 6. Other Material AI Industry News
- **2026-10-31 — OpenAI cuts its funding target by about $10 billion:** The Financial Times reported, relayed by Reuters and CNBC, that OpenAI trimmed its latest round to about $20 billion at a $1.25 trillion post-money valuation, with some investors reducing allocations amid a tech selloff. The round remains open and the terms are reported, not confirmed by OpenAI. Sources: [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/openai-cuts-funding-target-by-10-billion-ft-reports-2026-10-31/) · [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/openai-fundraising-20-billion-valuation.html) · [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/31/openai-reportedly-lowers-funding-target-for-new-round/).
- **2026-11-01 — Aramco closes a 49% stake in HUMAIN:** Aramco acquired 49% of the Saudi AI company, contributing about SAR 9.9 billion ($2.6 billion) in cash during 2026 plus AI, compute and digital assets; PIF retains 51%. HUMAIN targets 3 GW of AI data-centre capacity by 2030. Sources: [Aramco](https://www.aramco.com/en/news-media/news/2026/pif-and-aramco-close-humain-transaction-to-accelerate-humains-global-growth) · [PIF](https://www.pif.gov.sa/en/news-and-insights/press-releases/2026/pif-and-aramco-close-humain-transaction-to-accelerate-humain-global-growth/).
- **2026-11-02 — South Korea proposes a record AI budget:** President Lee Jae Myung proposed a 2027 budget with about $15.97 billion (21.3 trillion won) for AI, semiconductors, "physical AI" and data centres, nearly double 2026, described as the country's three megaprojects. Sources: [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/south-koreas-lee-vows-make-bold-ai-investment-record-budget-push-2026-11-02/) · [Inside AI](https://insideai.news/news/ai-policy-and-regulation/south-korea-ai-budget/14262/).

## Editorial Notes
- **Reported, not confirmed:** OpenAI's reduced funding target and $1.25 trillion valuation come from the Financial Times via Reuters and CNBC; the round is still open and OpenAI has not confirmed the figures. Samsung's account of the Altman meeting is the company's own; Musk's Grok Bot remark is a single X post with no figures. Vendor benchmark, price and cost figures — LongCat-2.5 specs and pricing, Carbon-X's scores and 1/1,800 cost claim, EditAgent's and HairDeck's results, Apriel Voice's scores, and Heretic's star and download counts — are the developers' own unless noted, and were not independently reproduced here.
- **Dates and windows:** every item was first announced or materially updated inside the primary window, 2026-10-31T06:19:49Z–2026-11-02T06:19:49Z. Paper dates follow Hugging Face Daily Papers for 2 November; a few were posted to arXiv slightly earlier (Apriel Voice, 29 October; EditAgent, 29 October; CaPtain, 29 October; Wizard, 29 October; R²Orch, 22 October). Repository star counts were read from GitDiscover for the week of 2026-11-01 and move quickly; entries marked "See repo" have unverified licences. LongCat-2.5's exact active-parameter count and licence were not yet published; Meituan says GitHub and Hugging Face releases will follow.
- **No backfill:** nothing in the 2026-10-24–2026-10-31 recovery window met the narrow bar for a consequential acquisition, funding round, model release or regulatory decision that was also absent from the last two briefings.
- **Verified but trimmed under limits:** SenseTime's open-weight SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview and Google's in-chat document editor both surfaced around 29–30 October, just before the window; a tampered Claude Code extension in the Cursor marketplace (event 29 October), the NAACP Clean Air Act ruling against xAI (30 October), S&P's negative outlook on Meta (30 October) and BeiJing-based GenRobot AI's $100 million Series A+ (disclosed 2 November) also fell short of the section limits here.
